title: SNAcc: An Open-Source Framework for Streaming-based Network-to-Storage Accelerators
problem: General purpose CPUs struggle to keep up with current Ethernet line speeds in network-to-storage pipelines, wasting compute resources and bandwidth for storage management.
motivation: FPGAs have wide data paths suitable for network applications; need framework for seamless integration of FPGA-based accelerators with network and storage without CPU bottleneck.
method: The framework uses an FPGA (a programmable hardware chip) to connect incoming network data directly to storage drives (NVMe SSDs) without going through the CPU. The FPGA acts as a bridge that moves data and performs processing tasks—like classifying images from the stream—without the main processor getting involved. This works because FPGAs can handle the sustained high-speed data flow that would slow down a general-purpose CPU.
key_novelty: It connects 100G Ethernet directly to SSD storage via FPGA, allowing both the network and storage to hit their maximum speed limits simultaneously without the CPU getting in the way.
contributions: Open-source framework for FPGA network-to-storage accelerators
Direct PCIe NVMe access without CPU intervention
Bandwidth saturation demonstration for network and storage
